Capture-recapture assumes every edge is equally catchable. Curation is biased to
well-studied genes, so rarely-studied edges are under-caught in EVERY catalogue at
once. That inflates the overlap and DEFLATES N, so all three estimates are lower
bounds and the true edge count is above even the highest of them.
The extrapolation assumes missing edges attach like observed ones. They do not:
curated edges concentrate on studied hubs, and loop 202 measured that evidence
CLUSTERS (both-E3 at 0.2215 against p^2 of 0.0686). Clustered missing edges would
make fewer new motifs than the exponent predicts, so the projections above are
upper bounds in that direction while being lower bounds in the direction above.
Those two biases point opposite ways and this design cannot net them out.
A cell does not run all its edges at once. These counts are of a static wiring
diagram pooled over cell types; loop 187's curated and binding tiers already
disagreed on feedforward by 22 sigma, which is what pooling looks like.
